# D11 Lowen Quay, PWL: 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-24

## What the data shows

| Channel | Typical weekly level (Oct to early Nov) | Weeks of 11-10 / 11-17 / 11-24 | Change | Week of 12-01 onward |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Counter | 83–93 (avg ≈ 88) | 132 / 131 / 126 (avg ≈ 130) | ≈ +47% | 82–88 |
| Online | 39–42 (avg ≈ 41) | 59 / 61 / 57 (avg ≈ 59) | ≈ +45% | 36–42 |
| Contract | 49–143, swinging widely | 135 / 135 / 129 | Within normal range | 88–137 |

- Counter and online rose by a similar proportion at the same time, held for exactly three weeks, and dropped back together.
- Contract shows nothing clearly unusual. It varies a lot week to week, and these three values fall inside its normal range.

## Context checks

- **Other West depots:** D10 Abermoor and D12 Carrick Stowe show no matching three-week rise. D10 was actually lower in the week of 11-10 (243). So this looks specific to D11, at least within the West depots shown.
- **Pricing:** No price list changes in 2025, so pricing doesn't explain it.
- **Staff notes:** None mention D11 or any West depot.
- **Data loading:** No weekly files were missing, so this isn't a gap or partial load in the data.

## What I can't tell you

The data doesn't show **why** this happened. Nothing provided (prices, notes, or other depots) explains a temporary rise in walk-in and online demand at D11 during those weeks. Possible causes such as a local project, an event, or a competitor's outage could fit, but none is supported by the data. Asking the D11 depot staff would be the most direct way to find out.
